deities: Mata Tripurmalini (Goddess Durga; the temple is counted among the 51 Shakti Peethas - the site where Sati's right breast is believed to have fallen)
Kali (shrine adjacent to the main sanctum)
Lord Shiva (large seated statue in the centre of the talab, water spouting like a fountain)
Shiva lingam in the replica Amarnath Cave, plus figurines and paintings of many Hindu deities
festivals: Shri Harballabh Sangeet Sammelan (annual classical music festival in December; one of India's oldest, established 1875; Ravi Shankar performed here in 1977)

history.period: About 200 years old (per Expedia - verify); the talab described as ancient
history.summary: The Shri Devi Talab Mandir on Tanda Road is one of Jalandhar's premier Hindu temples and a 51-Shakti-Peetha shrine to Mata Tripurmalini. Its focal point is a large talab (sacred tank) ringed by a broad causeway where worshippers meditate; in the centre stands a seated Lord Shiva statue from which water spouts like a fountain. The complex includes the main Mata Tripurmalini shrine, an adjacent Kali monument, a large replica of the Amarnath Cave (entered via a footpath lined with tiger statues, housing a Shiva lingam, figurines and paintings), and a mock mountain decorated with giant-sized gods, lions and tigers including a lion's head visitors can step into. A Panjab University academic paper counts Devi Talab among the 51 Shakti Pithas. In December the temple hosts the Harballabh Sangeet Sammelan classical music festival. The Shri Devi Talab Mandir Charitable Hospital stands on Mandir Marg nearby. The temple's prabandhak committee keeps the ancient pond's water clean with an eco-friendly liquid treatment (OXIBON, with BioTic), preserving aquatic life without chemicals. NOTE: CSV row 813 ('Devi Talab Mandir', Ludhiana) appears to be a duplicate/CSV error for this same temple - see 813.json.

name: Shri Devi Talab Mandir
town_description: Jalandhar is one of Punjab's oldest cities, with roots in the Indus Valley Civilization period, historically linked to the Nath tradition and the Shakta cult. The Devi Talab Mandir on Tanda Road, about 1 km from the railway station, is the city's most famous Shakti shrine.

travel.airport: Sri Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport, Amritsar (~80 km); Adampur domestic airport is closer (~25 km, limited service - verify).
travel.railway: Jalandhar City Junction on the Delhi-Amritsar line, about 1 km from the temple.
travel.road: On NH-44; well connected to Amritsar (80 km), Ludhiana (60 km) and Delhi (375 km). The temple is on Tanda Road, reached by auto/taxi.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; December for the Harballabh Sangeet Sammelan; Navratri for festivals.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Listed as open daily 5:00 AM to 10:00 PM (verify - per devitalabmandir.com listing). Free entry.
